findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() — unwrap() on an IO result in production code will panic on any file-system error (missing file, permission denied, truncated).
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted or absent file path causes process abort instead of returning a typed, recoverable error.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> or a domain error type. Propagate with ? or explicit match/map_err.

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() — unwrap() on a parse result in production code will panic on any non-numeric input in the second CSV field.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV line (non-numeric value field) causes process abort instead of returning a typed parse error.
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> from the inner closure via try_fold or map_err on .parse(), propagating parse failures as typed errors.

findings.problem: parse::<u32>().unwrap() as u16 — lossy as conversion from u32 to u16 after unwrap. Values above 65535 silently truncate.
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value in range 65536..=u32::MAX silently truncates to a wrong u16 value instead of being rejected.
findings.fix: Parse directly as u16 via .parse::<u16>() or use u32::try_into().map_err() to return a typed overflow error.

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] — unchecked indexing into a Vec of unknown length. If a CSV line has fewer than 2 comma-separated fields, this panics.
findings.failure_mode: Malformed CSV line with fewer than 2 fields causes index-out-of-bounds panic in production.
findings.fix: Use get(0)/get(1) with map_err, or destructuring match on the parts slice, returning a typed error for malformed lines.

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) — hidden I/O/side effect inside a data-loading function that appears to be a pure transformation. Violates the functional core / imperative shell boundary.
findings.failure_mode: The function has observable side effects (stdout writes) that cannot be suppressed in tests, and the function is no longer deterministic or referentially transparent. Logging is mixed into data-parsing logic.
findings.fix: Remove println! from the core parsing loop. Return audit events or a count separately if needed. Push all I/O (printing, file reads) to the imperative shell layer.

findings.problem: load_audits returns Vec<Record> directly (fallible result), absorbing IO and parse failures silently via unwrap. The function signature promises success but can panic on any failure.
findings.failure_mode: Callers have no way to distinguish between zero records (valid) and load failure (error). API contract is broken.
findings.fix: Change signature to pub fn load_audits(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> or a domain-specific error enum. Use ? and try_fold to propagate errors.

findings.problem: Collecting all split parts into Vec<String> when only two fields are needed. split_once would avoid the intermediate allocation.
findings.failure_mode: Wasted heap allocation and CPU per line. For large audit files this compounds unnecessarily.
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').map(|(name, value)| ...) instead of splitting all parts into a Vec.

findings.problem: No checked arithmetic or bounds validation on the parsed value before the as u16 cast. The intermediate u32 parse could yield values outside u16 range.
findings.failure_mode: Silent truncation of valid numeric values that exceed u16::MAX.
findings.fix: Parse as u16 directly: .parse::<u16>() or use .parse::<u32>().and_then(|v| u16::try_from(v).map_err(...)).
